Reproducing Gillon, Lecoq et al. (2023) from dandiset 000037¶

Paper. Gillon CJ, Lecoq JA, Pina JE, et al. (2023). Responses of pyramidal cell somata and apical dendrites in mouse visual cortex over multiple days. Scientific Data 10, 287. doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02214-y. A data descriptor. The claims file (claims/000037/10.1038-s41597-023-02214-y.yaml) was written from the version of record as served by Europe PMC (PMC10192216), with Supplementary Table 1 read as metadata.csv of the authors' metadata repository.

Dandiset. DANDI:000037, version 0.230426.0054. The paper cites this version: its reference 13 carries the DOI 10.48324/DANDI.000037/0.230426.0054 (in the Crossref record of the article; the Europe PMC text prints the reference without it). The later version 0.240209.1623 holds the same 150 NWB files with the same blobs, and adds a CHANGES file and links to the papers in its metadata (shown in the data check). Only the basic files (behavior+ophys) are opened; each is streamed into memory once and nothing is written to disk.

Outside inputs, all pinned and named in the helper openscope_ca.py: Supplementary Table 1 (metadata.csv of jeromelecoq/allen_openscope_metadata at commit 0e9c7ac), used for Tables 1 and 2 and for the local session numbers and QC results that select the paper's 33 analysed sessions; and from the paper's repository colleenjg/OpenScope_CA_Analysis at commit 046e7fe, the ROI matching files of the Fig. 8 example mice and the source data of Fig. 7a. Supplementary Table 1 agrees with Tables 1 and 2 of the paper text in every field (checked while preparing this entry, not run here).

qc-failures blocked: no QC status in the dataset

fig8-somata-less-order-dependent blocked: per-ordering counts published for two mice only

fig5-consistent-vs-inconsistent tested; blocked as it depends on fig5-example-responses
fig6-behaviour-all-mice tested
fig7a-snr-above-1 tested
fig7a-snr-stable, fig7b-signal-stable tested; blocked, the criterion's readings disagree
fig7c-correlations-similar tested; blocked, the criterion's readings disagree
fig7c-high-correlation-fraction tested; blocked as it depends on fig7c-correlations-similar
fig7a-source-link (with the paper's Fig. 7a source data) tested
fig9-onset-offset-transients tested
file-sizes, download-33-files tested

The analysis streams about 25 GB and takes about 11 minutes (cell 2 prints the time taken to stream and reduce the files).

import ast
import time
import warnings

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats

import openscope_ca as oc

pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
In [2]:
# LOAD-CELL: stream the 50 basic files once each and reduce them to what the claims use.
started = time.time()
assets = oc.version_assets()
latest = oc.version_assets(oc.LATEST_VERSION)
supp = oc.supplementary_table()
supp["session_id"] = supp.session_id.astype(str)
supp["subject_id"] = supp.subject_id.astype(str)
basic = assets[assets.kind == "B"].reset_index(drop=True)
basic["url"] = oc.run_parallel(oc.s3_url, basic.asset_id.tolist(), workers=8)
basic = basic.merge(supp[["session_id", "local_session_n", "QC"]], left_on="session",
                    right_on="session_id", how="left")
# The paper's analyses use local sessions 1 to 3 that passed QC (Supplementary Table 1), as the
# claims file states; correlations are computed for those, Fig. 5 measures for their session 1.
basic["analysed"] = (basic.local_session_n <= 3) & (basic.QC == "passed")
order = np.argsort(basic["size"].to_numpy())[::-1]


def job(i):
    r = basic.iloc[i]
    return oc.analyse(r.url, masks=True, corr=bool(r.analysed),
                      fig5=bool(r.analysed and r.local_session_n == 1))


done = oc.run_parallel(job, order.tolist(), weights=basic["size"].to_numpy()[order] / 1e9,
                       workers=4, budget=3.0)
S, R = {}, {}
for k, i in enumerate(order):
    S[basic.session[i]], R[basic.session[i]] = done[k]
print(f"streamed {len(S)} basic files ({basic['size'].sum() / 1e9:.1f} GB) of dandiset "
      f"{oc.DANDISET_ID} version {oc.DANDISET_VERSION} in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

streamed 50 basic files (25.2 GB) of dandiset 000037 version 0.230426.0054 in 667 s

rows = []
for sid, s in S.items():
    loc = ast.literal_eval(s["location"]) if s["location"].startswith("{") else {}
    start = pd.Timestamp(s["session_start_time"])
    rows.append({
        "session": sid, "subject": s["subject_id"], "identifier": s["identifier"],
        "start": s["session_start_time"], "date_file": start.strftime("%Y%m%d"),
        # The same clock read as UTC (Supplementary Table 1 gives these clock values as UTC),
        # converted to the Allen Institute's time zone.
        "date_if_utc": start.tz_localize(None).tz_localize("UTC").tz_convert("America/Los_Angeles").strftime("%Y%m%d"),
        "start_naive": start.tz_localize(None),
        "area": loc.get("area"), "depth": int(loc.get("depth")), "genotype": s["genotype"],
        "sex": s["sex"], "age_days": int(s["age"].strip("PD")), "species": s["species"],
        "n_rois": s["dff_shape"][1], "n_frames": s["dff_shape"][0],
        "n_tracked": int(np.isfinite(s["tracking_id"]).sum()),
        "imaging_rate_stated": s["imaging_rate"], "fps_2p": 1 / np.median(np.diff(s["dff_t"])),
        "fps_run": 1 / np.median(np.diff(s["run_t"])), "fps_pupil": 1 / np.median(np.diff(s["pupil_t"])),
        "indicator": s["indicator"], "excitation_nm": s["excitation_lambda"],
        "mask_shape": s["mask_shape"][1:], "max_proj_shape": s["max_projection_shape"]})
sess = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["subject", "start_naive"]).set_index("session")
sess["line"] = sess.genotype.map(lambda g: "L2/3" if g.startswith("Cux2") else "L5" if g.startswith("Rbp4") else "?")
# Plane from the recorded depth: layer 1 (dendrites) at 20 to 75 um, cell body layers at 175 and 375 um (Methods).
sess["plane"] = np.where(sess.depth < 100, "D", "S")
sess["group"] = sess.line + "-" + sess.plane
sess["local_n"] = sess.groupby("subject").cumcount() + 1
sess = sess.join(supp.set_index("session_id")[["local_session_n", "QC", "imaging_plane", "imaging_cell_layer"]])
sess["analysed"] = (sess.local_n <= 3) & (sess.QC == "passed")
print("Subjects:", sess.subject.nunique(), "; sessions:", len(sess), "; species:", sess.species.unique().tolist())
print("Session id equals file identifier and the id in the file name:", bool((sess.index == sess.identifier).all()))
print("Chronological session number equals Supplementary Table 1's local session number:",
      bool((sess.local_n == sess.local_session_n).all()))
print("Plane from depth equals Supplementary Table 1's plane:",
      bool((sess.plane.map({"D": "distal_apical_dendrites", "S": "somata"}) == sess.imaging_plane).all()))
print("Layer from genotype equals Supplementary Table 1's layer:", bool((sess.line == sess.imaging_cell_layer).all()))
print("\nSessions per subject and group:")
print(sess.groupby(["group", "subject"]).size().to_string())
print("\nAnalysed sessions (local 1 to 3, passed QC):", int(sess.analysed.sum()), "from",
      sess[sess.analysed].subject.nunique(), "mice")
print(sess[["subject", "group", "start", "depth", "sex", "age_days", "n_rois", "n_tracked", "local_n", "QC"]].to_string())

The stated imaging rate (30 Hz) agrees with the timestamps (about 30.1 Hz), running is sampled at 60 Hz and pupil at the imaging rate. Running velocity is stated in cm/s, and its values (session medians of 0.007 to 33 cm/s, with a median of 0.08 cm/s over sessions, and 99th percentiles of 2 to 68 cm/s) are consistent with that, not shown by it. Pupil diameter is stated in mm, with medians under 1 mm; positions are within the 6.528 mm image width the files give. dF/F is stated as "Normalized fluorescence (A.U.)"; ROI medians near 0 are consistent with dF/F.

    t = S[sid]["trials"]
    tab.append({"session": sid, "rows": len(t), "grey": int((t.stimulus_type == "grayscreen").sum()),
                "gabor_images": int((t.stimulus_type == "gabors").sum()),
                "U_images": int((t.gabor_frame == "U").sum()),
                "flow_right": int((t.stimulus_template_name == "visflow_right").sum()),
                "flow_left": int((t.stimulus_template_name == "visflow_left").sum()),
                "flow_reversed": int(((t.stimulus_type == "visflow") & (t.unexpected == 1)).sum()),
                "first_stimulus": t.stimulus_template_name[t.stimulus_type != "grayscreen"].iloc[0],
                "stim_span_min": (t.stop_time.max() - t.start_time.min()) / 60})

Every session holds four grey screen periods around three stimulus periods (Gabor sequences, and visual flow in each direction), in an order that varies between sessions. The trial table has no stimulus seed column, and no QC field is in the files.

In [7]:
# Clock check. The trial table gives each grey screen transition as a two-photon frame. For each
# session, the population mean of the robust-scaled dF/F changes across the six transitions; the
# same contrast is computed with the transitions shifted in time by 10 to 300 s (500 shifts, fixed
# seed), which keeps the response shape but breaks the alignment.
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)


def transition_contrast(pop, frames, fps):
    w = int(round(fps))
    vals = [abs(pop[f:f + w].mean() - pop[f - w:f].mean()) for f in frames if f - w >= 0 and f + w <= len(pop)]
    return np.mean(vals)


clock = []
for sid in sess.index:
    pop, fr, fps = R[sid]["popmean_scaled"], R[sid]["transitions"].frame.to_numpy(), R[sid]["fps"]
    true = transition_contrast(pop, fr, fps)
    shifts = rng.uniform(10, 300, 500) * rng.choice([-1, 1], 500)
    null = np.array([transition_contrast(pop, fr + int(round(d * fps)), fps) for d in shifts])
    clock.append({"session": sid, "true": true, "null_median": np.median(null), "null_p99": np.percentile(null, 99),
                  "rank": (null >= true).mean()})
clock = pd.DataFrame(clock).set_index("session")
print(clock.round(4).to_string())
print("Sessions whose true contrast exceeds every shifted one:", int((clock["rank"] == 0).sum()), "of", len(clock))
print("Sessions with the true contrast below the 99th percentile of the shifted ones:",
      clock.index[clock.true <= clock.null_p99].tolist())
notes = supp.set_index("session_id")
print("Supplementary Table 1 QC and experimental notes of those sessions:")
print(notes.loc[clock.index[clock.true <= clock.null_p99], ["subject_id", "local_session_n", "QC", "experimental_notes"]].to_string())

The contrast at the true transitions is above every shifted contrast in 38 of 50 sessions, and above the 99th percentile of the shifted ones in 48. In those 48 sessions the dF/F shares the clock of the trial table. It is not established in two sessions: 777496949 (mouse 418779, 15 ROIs, rank 0.054) and 838633305 (440889 local session 6, which failed QC; Supplementary Table 1's experimental notes say the laser was set to 800 nm instead of 910 nm, printed above, though the file states 910 nm). The second is not among the 33 analysed sessions; the first is, and its group's results below are reported with the others. Running and pupil carry their own timestamps on the same time base; no stimulus contrast was used for them, so their alignment is stated, not shown.

# Recordings deposited twice: compare running traces, pupil traces, dF/F summaries and trial times
# of every pair of sessions.
sig = {}
for sid in sess.index:
    s = S[sid]
    sig[sid] = (np.round(s["run_v"][:5000], 6).tobytes(), np.round(np.nan_to_num(s["pupil_d"][:5000]), 6).tobytes(),
                np.round(R[sid]["roi"]["mean"].to_numpy(), 6).tobytes(), np.round(s["trials"].start_time.to_numpy(), 4).tobytes())
pairs = []
ids = list(sig)
for i in range(len(ids)):
    for j in range(i + 1, len(ids)):
        same = [a == b for a, b in zip(sig[ids[i]], sig[ids[j]])]
        if any(same):
            pairs.append((ids[i], ids[j], same))
print("Pairs of sessions sharing running, pupil, dF/F means or trial times:", pairs if pairs else "none")
print("Pairs with the same ROI count:",
      [(a, b) for a, b in zip(sess.index[:-1], sess.index[1:]) if sess.n_rois[a] == sess.n_rois[b]])

table1-subjects¶

The dataset holds 13 mice whose subject ids, sex, date of birth, imaged cell type (L2/3 or L5 pyramidal) and imaging plane (somata or distal apical dendrites) are as listed in Table 1.

Table 1's values are taken from Supplementary Table 1 (metadata.csv, which holds the columns of Tables 1 and 2). The files record sex and genotype (cell type through the line); they record no date of birth and no plane, which are listed and also shown as values implied by the recorded age and depth.

table2-sessions¶

The 50 sessions have the subject ids, session ids, imaging dates, imaging depths, ROI counts, tracked ROI counts, QC results and stimulus seeds listed in Table 2.

Table 2's values are taken from Supplementary Table 1. The date of a session is the date of its start time as the file states it; the same clock read as UTC (as Supplementary Table 1 labels it) and converted to Pacific time is shown as a variant.

Result: not reproduced. All 50 sessions of Table 2 are in the dataset, and subject, ROI count and tracked ROI count agree for all 50. Only 43 of 50 agree in every recorded field, below the 45 the criterion asks for partial reproduction. The three sessions of mouse 433414 are recorded at a depth of 60 um where Table 2 gives 75. Four sessions (412933 local session 3 and the three of 418779) start one day later in the files than the date in Table 2. Their start times are early-morning clock values (00:18 to 03:01) stated with a Pacific offset (for example 2018-10-19T00:18-07:00); read as UTC, the same clock values fall on the evening of the day before in Pacific time. Supplementary Table 1 gives the same clock values as UTC for all 50 sessions. Read as UTC, all 50 dates agree and 47 of 50 sessions agree in every field (the depth difference remains). The UTC reading is not one the criterion gives, so it is a variant and does not decide the outcome. The files hold no other wall-clock time that could settle which reading is right: timestamps_reference_time equals session_start_time, and file_create_date gives the conversion dates (2022 and 2023). The depth difference of 433414 holds under either reading. The files do not record QC or the stimulus seed.

qc-failures¶

Two animals had at least one session that failed the Allen Institute's QC thresholds, and some animals had more than three sessions, for example when an early session failed QC.

Blocked: the files hold no QC status, and the criterion blocks the claim when the dataset records none. The counts from Supplementary Table 1 are shown for reference only.

Result: blocked (metadata_insufficient). None of the 50 files holds a QC field: not in the trial table or subject fields, and none of the 23 small datasets and attributes under general and at each file's top level mentions QC, quality, pass, fail, exclusion or rejection (all of them are printed for 759666166, a failed session of 411400). For reference only, Supplementary Table 1 gives 3 animals with any failed session (reading a) and 2 whose first three sessions failed (reading b). The part of the claim the files can test holds: 5 animals have more than three sessions (411400, 412933, 433448, 433458, 440889).

session-schedule¶

Each mouse had three 70-minute imaging sessions within three to six days, with at most one session per day.

The criterion's four combinations: sessions (i) local 1 to 3, or (ii) the sessions of the paper's analyses (local 1 to 3 passing QC, or local 4 to 6 for mice 411400 and 412933); span (a) days from first to third session (3 to 6 allowed), or (b) calendar days counted inclusively (3 to 6 allowed). Dates are those of the start times as the files state them; the clock read as UTC is a variant.

In [15]:
def schedule(date_col):
    out = []
    for subj, g in sess.groupby("subject"):
        sets = {"i": g[g.local_n <= 3]}
        sets["ii"] = g[g.local_n >= 4] if subj in ("411400", "412933") else g[g.analysed]
        for k, sub in sets.items():
            d = pd.to_datetime(sub[date_col]).sort_values()
            span = (d.iloc[-1] - d.iloc[0]).days
            out.append({"subject": subj, "sessions": k, "dates": " ".join(sub[date_col]),
                        "span_a": span, "span_b": span + 1, "shared_date": d.duplicated().any(),
                        "all_dates_distinct_in_mouse": not pd.to_datetime(g[date_col]).duplicated().any()})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


for date_col in ("date_file", "date_if_utc"):
    sch = schedule(date_col)
    print(f"Dates from {date_col}:")
    print(sch.to_string(index=False))
    for k in ("i", "ii"):
        for span in ("span_a", "span_b"):
            sub = sch[sch.sessions == k]
            ok = sub[span].between(3, 6) & ~sub.shared_date
            print(f"  sessions ({k}), span ({span[-1]}): mice meeting it {int(ok.sum())} of {len(sub)}; failing:",
                  sub.subject[~ok].tolist())
    print()
dur = pd.Series({sid: (S[sid]["trials"].stop_time.max() - S[sid]["trials"].start_time.min()) / 60 for sid in sess.index})
rec = sess.n_frames / sess.fps_2p / 60
print("Session duration from the stimulus table (min):", dur.min().round(2), "to", dur.max().round(2),
      "; two-photon recording (min):", rec.min().round(2), "to", rec.max().round(2), "; within 70 +/- 7:",
      bool(dur.between(63, 77).all() and rec.between(63, 77).all()))

Result: reproduced. Under combination (i)(b), local sessions 1 to 3 with calendar days counted inclusively, all 13 mice have spans of 3 to 6 days with no two sessions on one date. imaging-depths¶

Somata were imaged at 175 um (L2/3) and 375 um (L5) depth, and distal apical dendrites at 50 to 75 um (L2/3) and 20 um (L5).

In [16]:
# For L2/3 dendrites the criterion admits any depth from 50 to 75 um inclusive (answer of 2026-10-22).
allowed = {"L2/3-S": lambda d: d == 175, "L5-S": lambda d: d == 375, "L2/3-D": lambda d: 50 <= d <= 75, "L5-D": lambda d: d == 20}
sess["depth_ok"] = [allowed[g](d) for d, g in zip(sess.depth, sess.group)]
print(sess.groupby(["group", "depth"]).size().rename("sessions").to_string())
print("Sessions whose depth is the value for their line and plane (50 to 75 um for L2/3 dendrites):", int(sess.depth_ok.sum()), "of 50")
print("Sessions that do not:", sess[~sess.depth_ok][["subject", "group", "depth"]].to_dict("index"))
print("Sessions at exactly 50 or 75 um among L2/3 dendrites (the earlier criterion):",
      int(sum(d in (50, 75) for d, g in zip(sess.depth, sess.group) if g == "L2/3-D")), "of", int((sess.group == "L2/3-D").sum()))

Result: reproduced. All 50 sessions are at the depth the criterion gives for their line and plane: 175 and 375 um for somata, 20 um for L5 dendrites, and from 50 to 75 um for L2/3 dendrites. The three sessions of L2/3 dendritic mouse 433414 are at 60 um, inside that range. An earlier reading of the criterion allowed only 50 or 75 um. The answer of 2026-10-22 replaced it with the range, which turned the result from not reproduced into reproduced. Table 2 gives 75 um for these sessions, so the dataset and the paper disagree on this depth (table2-sessions).

acquisition-rates¶

Calcium movies were recorded at 30 Hz over a 400 um field of view at 512 x 512 pixels, and running was recorded at 60 Hz in cm/s.

roi-noise-rejection¶

ROIs that were too noisy, with a mean dF/F below 0 or a median dF/F above the midpoint between the trace's minimum and maximum, were rejected, so no retained ROI has either property.

In [18]:
noise = []
for sid in sess.index:
    r = R[sid]["roi"]
    mid = (r["min"] + r["max"]) / 2
    noise.append({"session": sid, "group": sess.group[sid], "rois": len(r), "mean_below_0": int((r["mean"] < 0).sum()),
                  "median_above_midrange": int((r["median"] > mid).sum()),
                  "either": int(((r["mean"] < 0) | (r["median"] > mid)).sum()),
                  "lowest_mean": r["mean"].min(), "highest_median_minus_mid": (r["median"] - mid).max()})
noise = pd.DataFrame(noise).set_index("session")
print(noise.to_string())
print("ROIs with either property:", noise.either.sum(), "of", noise.rois.sum(),
      f"({100 * noise.either.sum() / noise.rois.sum():.3f}%)", "; sessions with any:", int((noise.either > 0).sum()))

roi-count-ranges¶

Somatic planes yielded 15 to 224 ROIs per mouse per session and dendritic planes 159 to 1636.

In [19]:
readings = {"(a) 33 analysed sessions": sess.analysed, "(b) all sessions passing QC": sess.QC == "passed",
            "(c) all 50 sessions": pd.Series(True, index=sess.index)}
lim = {"S": ((15, 1.5), (224, 22.4)), "D": ((159, 15.9), (1636, 163.6))}
for name, sel in readings.items():
    ok_all = True
    for plane in ("S", "D"):
        n = sess[sel & (sess.plane == plane)].n_rois
        (lo, tlo), (hi, thi) = lim[plane]
        ok = abs(n.min() - lo) <= tlo and abs(n.max() - hi) <= thi
        ok_all &= ok
        print(f"{name}, {'somata' if plane == 'S' else 'dendrites'}: {len(n)} sessions, {n.min()} to {n.max()} "
              f"(expected {lo} +/- {tlo} to {hi} +/- {thi}): {'within' if ok else 'outside'}")
    print(f"  {name}: {'all within tolerance' if ok_all else 'not all within tolerance'}")

tracked-roi-totals¶

Matching produced 254 tracked ROIs in L2/3 dendritic planes, 261 in L2/3 somatic, 516 in L5 dendritic and 129 in L5 somatic, about 100 to 500 per plane and about 32 to 75% of the theoretical maximum number of trackable ROIs.

In [20]:
trk = sess[sess.n_tracked > 0]
per_mouse = trk.groupby("subject").agg(group=("group", "first"), tracked=("n_tracked", "first"),
                                       tracked_sessions=("n_tracked", "size"), equal=("n_tracked", lambda v: v.nunique() == 1),
                                       min_rois=("n_rois", "min"), mean_rois=("n_rois", "mean"),
                                       local=("local_n", lambda v: sorted(v)))
print(per_mouse.to_string())
expected = {"L2/3-D": 254, "L2/3-S": 261, "L5-D": 516, "L5-S": 129}
for label, sel in (("11 mice of the paper's analyses", ~per_mouse.index.isin(["411400", "412933"])),
                   ("all 13 tracked mice (variant)", per_mouse.index == per_mouse.index)):
    pm = per_mouse[sel]
    tot = pm.groupby("group").agg(tracked=("tracked", "sum"), max_a=("min_rois", "sum"), max_b=("mean_rois", "sum"))
    tot["expected"] = pd.Series(expected)
    tot["pct_a"] = 100 * tot.tracked / tot.max_a
    tot["pct_b"] = 100 * tot.tracked / tot.max_b
    print(f"\n{label}:")
    print(tot.round(1).to_string())
    print("  totals equal the expected:", bool((tot.tracked == tot.expected).all()))
    for r in ("a", "b"):
        lo, hi = tot[f"pct_{r}"].min(), tot[f"pct_{r}"].max()
        print(f"  reading ({r}): lowest {lo:.1f}% (32 +/- 3.2), highest {hi:.1f}% (75 +/- 7.5):",
              "within" if abs(lo - 32) <= 3.2 and abs(hi - 75) <= 7.5 else "outside")

Result: reproduced. Over the 11 mice of the paper's analyses, the tracked ROIs sum to 254 (L2/3 dendrites), 261 (L2/3 somata), 516 (L5 dendrites) and 129 (L5 somata), as stated. With the theoretical maximum read as (a), the smallest ROI count of each mouse's three tracked sessions, the percentages run from 32.9% to 75.0%, within 32 +/- 3.2 and 75 +/- 7.5. Reading (b), the mean count, gives 25.4% to 65.7%, outside. Over all 13 tracked mice (variant) the dendritic totals are 352 and 678, which do not match.

tracked-sessions-overlap¶

The same imaging planes were recorded over three days and many ROIs could be identified in each day's recording, so that individual dendritic segments and somata can be followed over the three sessions.

The criterion is on the tracking indices. The mask centroids of tracked ROIs are added as a check that an index names the same place in the field of view in each session (not part of the criterion; the masks are not registered, so small shifts between sessions remain).

In [21]:
ov = []
for subj, g in trk.groupby("subject"):
    ids = [np.sort(S[sid]["tracking_id"][np.isfinite(S[sid]["tracking_id"])]) for sid in g.index]
    one_each = all(len(np.unique(i)) == len(i) for i in ids)
    same_set = all(np.array_equal(ids[0], i) for i in ids)
    c = [S[sid]["tracked_centroids"] for sid in g.index]
    d_same, d_other = [], []
    for a in range(len(c)):
        for b in range(a + 1, len(c)):
            ca, cb = c[a].to_numpy(), c[b].reindex(c[a].index).to_numpy()
            d_same.append(np.hypot(*(ca - cb).T))
            dist = np.hypot(ca[:, None, 0] - cb[None, :, 0], ca[:, None, 1] - cb[None, :, 1])
            np.fill_diagonal(dist, np.inf)
            d_other.append(dist.min(axis=1))
    d_same, d_other = np.concatenate(d_same), np.concatenate(d_other)
    ov.append({"subject": subj, "group": g.group.iloc[0], "sessions": len(g), "tracked": len(ids[0]),
               "equal_counts": len({len(i) for i in ids}) == 1, "each_index_once": one_each, "same_indices": same_set,
               "median_px_same_index": np.median(d_same), "median_px_nearest_other": np.median(d_other),
               "frac_same_closer": np.mean(d_same < d_other)})
ov = pd.DataFrame(ov).set_index("subject")
print(ov.round(2).to_string())
print("Tracked mice:", len(ov), "; with three sessions, equal counts, one-to-one indices:",
      int((ov.sessions.eq(3) & ov.equal_counts & ov.each_index_once & ov.same_indices).sum()))

Result: reproduced. All 13 tracked mice have three tracked sessions with equal numbers of tracked ROIs (12 to 353). In every one, each tracking index appears once per session and the three sessions carry the same indices. In the added mask check, the same index lies a median of 1.9 to 14.5 pixels apart between sessions, against 11.5 to 62.4 pixels to the nearest other tracked ROI. The same index is closer than any other tracked ROI for 55% (411400) to 100% of ROIs. The masks are not registered between sessions, so this check is consistent with the tracking, not a proof of it.

fig8a-final-matches and fig8b-final-matches¶

In the example L2/3 dendritic mouse of Fig. 8a, removing four conflicting pairwise matches from the union over session orderings left 136 final matches.

In the example L5 somatic mouse of Fig. 8b, removing two conflicting pairwise matches left 47 final matches.

fig8a-conflicts, fig8b-conflicts and fig8-somata-less-order-dependent¶

For the same mouse, the union of matches over all session orderings held four conflicting matches, which were removed.

For the same L5 somatic mouse, two conflicting matches were removed from the union over session orderings.

The number of matched ROIs varied less across session orderings for somata than for dendrites.

The union counts and the fewest and most matches over orderings come from the paper's roi_tracking/nway-matched-dfs files (commit in the helper); the tracked counts from the dataset.

The repository gives union counts of 140 (413663) and 49 (411771), so 140 - 136 = 4 and 49 - 47 = 2 conflicts, as stated. The repository's files hold per-ordering counts for these two mice only, so the comparison across mice cannot be made. In the two examples the range over orderings is 3 matches for the dendritic mouse (129 to 132, 2.2% of its final count) and 1 for the somatic mouse (47 to 48, 2.1%). That is smaller for somata in absolute terms but about equal as a fraction.

gabor-sequence-structure¶

Gabor sequences are repeating 1.5-s sequences of five 300-ms images (A-B-C-D-G), each non-grey image holding 30 Gabor patches, with inconsistent sequences replacing D by U, whose mean orientation is shifted by 90 degrees (drawn from 90, 135, 180 and 225 degrees, against 0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees for the other images).

In [24]:
gs = []
for sid in sess.index:
    g = S[sid]["trials"]
    g = g[g.stimulus_type == "gabors"].reset_index(drop=True)
    frames = g.gabor_frame.to_numpy()
    seqs = frames.reshape(-1, 5) if len(frames) % 5 == 0 else None
    order_ok = seqs is not None and all(tuple(r) in {("A", "B", "C", "D", "G"), ("A", "B", "C", "U", "G")} for r in seqs)
    dur = (g.stop_time - g.start_time).to_numpy()
    ori = g.gabor_mean_orientation.to_numpy().reshape(-1, 5)
    is_u = seqs[:, 3] == "U"
    abc_same = np.all(ori[:, :4][:, :3] == ori[:, [0]], axis=1)
    gs.append({"session": sid, "images": len(g), "sequences": len(seqs), "order_ok": order_ok,
               "dur_min": dur.min(), "dur_median": np.median(dur), "dur_max": dur.max(),
               "dur_within_10pct": np.mean((dur >= 0.27) & (dur <= 0.33)),
               "seq_dur_median": np.median(g.start_time.to_numpy()[5::5] - g.start_time.to_numpy()[:-5:5]),
               "patches": sorted(set(g.n_patches[g.gabor_frame != "G"])),
               "gabor_number": sorted(set(g.gabor_number.dropna())),
               "ABCD_oris": sorted(set(ori[:, :3].ravel()) | set(ori[~is_u, 3])),
               "U_oris": sorted(set(ori[is_u, 3])),
               "U_is_seq_plus_90": bool(np.all(ori[is_u, 3] == ori[is_u, 0] + 90)),
               "ABC_share_mean": bool(abc_same.all()), "kappa": sorted(set(g.gabor_kappa))})
gs = pd.DataFrame(gs).set_index("session")
print(gs.drop(columns=["patches", "gabor_number", "ABCD_oris", "U_oris", "kappa"]).round(4).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. In all 50 sessions the 1360 sequences follow A-B-C-D-G or A-B-C-U-G, every non-grey image holds 30 Gabor patches, A to D take mean orientations 0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees, and U takes 90, 135, 180 and 225 degrees, always the sequence's mean plus 90. Image durations have a median of 300 ms. Every image lies within 300 ms +/- 10% in 46 of 50 sessions. Four sessions hold 1 to 5 images outside it (up to 604 ms), 13 of 340000 images in all; the three sessions of mouse 411400 among them failed QC, and Supplementary Table 1's experimental notes record dropped stimulus frames for them (printed above). The criterion asks for every image in every session, so the duration part holds in 46 of 50 sessions. The criterion names no partial outcome; the claim holds in part, which is the protocol's partially reproduced, and a strict reading that admits only reproduced or not would give not reproduced.

visual-flow-structure¶

Visual flow is 105 white squares of 8 by 8 degrees moving at 50 degrees per second, in two consecutive periods (rightward and leftward) in random order, with 25% of squares reversed for 2 to 4 s during inconsistent flow.

In [25]:
vf = []
for sid in sess.index:
    t = S[sid]["trials"].reset_index(drop=True)
    v = t[t.stimulus_type == "visflow"]
    dirs = v.main_flow_direction.to_numpy()
    changes = int((dirs[1:] != dirs[:-1]).sum())
    contiguous = all(np.all(np.diff(v.index[v.main_flow_direction == d]) == 1) for d in set(dirs))
    runs = []
    for d in set(dirs):
        u = v[v.main_flow_direction == d].unexpected.to_numpy()
        dd = v[v.main_flow_direction == d]
        edges = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(np.concatenate([[0], u, [0]])))
        for a, b in zip(edges[::2], edges[1::2]):
            runs.append(dd.stop_time.iloc[b - 1] - dd.start_time.iloc[a])
    sq = S[sid]["squares"]
    speed = {}
    for k, (x, y, d) in sq.items():
        dx = np.diff(x.astype(float), axis=1)
        step = np.median(np.abs(dx[np.abs(dx) < 100]))           # px per stimulus frame (60 Hz), wraps excluded
        speed[k] = step * 60
        speed[k + "_dir"] = d
        # Squares moving against the main flow at the trial's first frame (reversed squares that
        # leave the screen re-enter with the main flow, so the fraction falls later in the trial).
        moving = np.where(np.abs(dx[:, 0]) < 100, np.sign(dx[:, 0]), 0)
        speed[k + "_frac_against"] = np.mean(moving == -np.sign(np.median(dx)))
    vf.append({"session": sid, "squares": sorted(set(v.square_number)), "size_px": sorted(set(v.square_size)),
               "flipped": sorted(set(v.square_proportion_flipped)), "direction_changes": changes,
               "periods_contiguous": contiguous, "first_direction": dirs[0],
               "reversal_min_s": min(runs), "reversal_max_s": max(runs), "reversals": len(runs),
               "speed_px_s": speed["consistent"], "frac_squares_against_in_reversal": speed["inconsistent_frac_against"]})
vf = pd.DataFrame(vf).set_index("session")
print(vf.drop(columns=["squares", "size_px", "flipped"]).round(3).to_string())
print("\nSquares:", {str(x) for x in vf.squares}, "; size (px):", {str(x) for x in vf.size_px},
      "; proportion reversed:", {str(x) for x in vf.flipped})
print("Sessions with two consecutive direction periods:", int(((vf.direction_changes == 1) & vf.periods_contiguous).sum()),
      "; first direction:", vf.first_direction.value_counts().to_dict())
print("Reversal durations (s):", vf.reversal_min_s.min().round(3), "to", vf.reversal_max_s.max().round(3))
print("Square speed (px/s):", vf.speed_px_s.min(), "to", vf.speed_px_s.max(), "; speed / size (1/s):",
      (vf.speed_px_s / 128).min(), "to", (vf.speed_px_s / 128).max(), "; paper 50 deg/s over 8 deg =", 50 / 8)
print("Fraction of squares moving against the flow at the first frame of the first reversed trial:",
      vf.frac_squares_against_in_reversal.min().round(3), "to", vf.frac_squares_against_in_reversal.max().round(3),
      "; median", vf.frac_squares_against_in_reversal.median().round(3), "; mean", vf.frac_squares_against_in_reversal.mean().round(3))
print("Not recorded: square size and speed in degrees (the table gives pixels of the unwarped stimulus).")

session-stimulus-durations¶

Each imaging session lasted 70 min, with 34 min of Gabor sequences and 17 min of visual flow in each direction, each stimulus period flanked by 30 s of grey screen.

inconsistent-fractions¶

Inconsistent sequences make up about 7% of Gabor sequences and 5% of visual flow time.

inconsistent-blocks¶

Each session is divided into about 30 blocks, each of 30 to 90 s of consistent stimulus followed by 3 to 6 s (Gabor) or 2 to 4 s (visual flow) of inconsistent stimulus, in multiples of 1.5 s (Gabor) and 1 s (visual flow).

A block is a run of consistent stimulus followed by a run of inconsistent stimulus, within one stimulus period. Gabor runs are counted in sequences (the unexpected flag is set for the whole A-B-C-U-G sequence), flow runs in 1-s trials.

In [28]:
blocks = []
for sid in sess.index:
    t = S[sid]["trials"]
    for name in ("gabors", "visflow_right", "visflow_left"):
        x = t[t.stimulus_template_name == name]
        if name == "gabors":
            x = x[x.gabor_frame == "A"]                          # one row per sequence
            ends = t[(t.stimulus_template_name == name) & (t.gabor_frame == "G")].stop_time.to_numpy()
        else:
            ends = x.stop_time.to_numpy()
        u, st = x.unexpected.to_numpy(), x.start_time.to_numpy()
        i = 0
        while i < len(u):
            j = i
            while j < len(u) and u[j] == 0:
                j += 1
            k = j
            while k < len(u) and u[k] == 1:
                k += 1
            if k > j:   # a consistent run followed by an inconsistent run
                blocks.append({"session": sid, "stimulus": name, "consistent_s": st[j] - st[i], "inconsistent_s": ends[k - 1] - st[j],
                               "n_units_inconsistent": k - j, "n_units_consistent": j - i})
            i = k if k > i else i + 1
blocks = pd.DataFrame(blocks)
blocks["kind"] = np.where(blocks.stimulus == "gabors", "gabor", "flow")
inc_lim = {"gabor": (3 * 0.9, 6 * 1.1), "flow": (2 * 0.9, 4 * 1.1)}
blocks["consistent_ok"] = blocks.consistent_s.between(30 * 0.9, 90 * 1.1)
blocks["inconsistent_ok"] = [inc_lim[k][0] <= v <= inc_lim[k][1] for k, v in zip(blocks.kind, blocks.inconsistent_s)]
print(blocks.groupby("stimulus")[["consistent_s", "inconsistent_s"]].describe().round(2).T.to_string())
print("\nInconsistent runs, in units (Gabor sequences of 1.5 s, flow trials of 1 s):",
      blocks.groupby("kind").n_units_inconsistent.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
counts = {"(a) all stimuli": blocks.groupby("session").size(),
          "(b) Gabor": blocks[blocks.kind == "gabor"].groupby("session").size(),
          "(b) flow, both directions": blocks[blocks.kind == "flow"].groupby("session").size(),
          "(c) flow right": blocks[blocks.stimulus == "visflow_right"].groupby("session").size(),
          "(c) flow left": blocks[blocks.stimulus == "visflow_left"].groupby("session").size()}
for k, v in counts.items():
    print(f"{k}: mean blocks per session {v.mean():.2f} (range {v.min()} to {v.max()}); within 30 +/- 3: {abs(v.mean() - 30) <= 3}")
for kind in ("gabor", "flow"):
    b = blocks[blocks.kind == kind]
    print(f"{kind}: blocks with consistent and inconsistent durations in range (widened 10%): "

          f"inconsistent {100 * b.inconsistent_ok.mean():.1f}%)")
print("All blocks:", f"{100 * (blocks.consistent_ok & blocks.inconsistent_ok).mean():.1f}%")

fig5-example-responses¶

Both somatic and dendritic ROIs responded clearly to the Gabor and visual flow stimuli, many with increased fluorescence at stimulus onset.

Session 1 of the 11 mice of the paper's analyses. The selection is made within each mouse's session (helper select_gabor_rois and select_flow_rois), on robust-scaled dF/F; the selected ROIs are pooled per line and plane. Panels: (a) consistent sequences around D onset, (b) inconsistent sequences around U onset, (c) temporal-to-nasal (leftward) flow and (d) nasal-to-temporal (rightward) flow, around inconsistent flow onset.

In [29]:
s1 = sess[sess.analysed & (sess.local_n == 1)]
panels = {"a": ("gabor_D", "gabor_t"), "b": ("gabor_U", "gabor_t"), "c": ("flow_left", "flow_t"), "d": ("flow_right", "flow_t")}
groups = ["L2/3-D", "L2/3-S", "L5-D", "L5-S"]


def pooled(group, key, scaled="scaled", sel_key=None):
    """Selected ROIs' mean traces, pooled over the group's session-1 recordings, with the mouse of each."""
    traces, mouse = [], []
    for sid in s1.index[s1.group == group]:
        f5 = R[sid]["fig5"]
        sel = f5[f"{sel_key or key}_{scaled}_sel"]
        traces.append(f5[f"{key}_{scaled}_mean"][sel])
        mouse += [sess.subject[sid]] * len(sel)
    return np.concatenate(traces), np.array(mouse)


rows5, per_mouse5 = [], []
for scaled in ("scaled", "unscaled"):
    for p, (key, tkey) in panels.items():
        for grp in groups:
            tr, mouse = pooled(grp, key, scaled)
            t = R[s1.index[0]]["fig5"][tkey]
            pre = tr[:, t < 0].mean() if len(tr) else np.nan
            post = tr[:, t >= 0].mean() if len(tr) else np.nan
            rows5.append({"traces": scaled, "panel": p, "group": grp, "rois": len(tr), "mice": len(set(mouse)),
                          "pre": pre, "post": post, "post_minus_pre": post - pre, "higher_after": post > pre})
            for m in sorted(set(s1.subject[s1.group == grp])):
                sel = mouse == m
                per_mouse5.append({"traces": scaled, "panel": p, "group": grp, "mouse": m, "rois": int(sel.sum()),
                                   "post_minus_pre": (tr[sel][:, t >= 0].mean() - tr[sel][:, t < 0].mean()) if sel.any() else np.nan})
rows5 = pd.DataFrame(rows5)
print("Selected ROIs, robust-scaled dF/F (main):")
print(rows5[rows5.traces == "scaled"].round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nPer mouse (robust-scaled):")
print(pd.DataFrame(per_mouse5).query("traces == 'scaled'").pivot_table(index=["group", "mouse"], columns="panel",
      values=["rois", "post_minus_pre"]).round(3).to_string())
n_sess1 = {sid: (R[sid]["n_rois"], int(R[sid]["fig5"]["snr_above"].sum()), R[sid]["fig5"]["gabor_D_n"], R[sid]["fig5"]["gabor_U_n"],
                 R[sid]["fig5"]["flow_left_n"], R[sid]["fig5"]["flow_right_n"]) for sid in s1.index}
thr5 = pd.DataFrame([{"session": sid, "mouse": sess.subject[sid], "group": sess.group[sid], "selection": key,
                      **R[sid]["fig5"][f"{key}_scaled_thr"], "selected": len(R[sid]["fig5"][f"{key}_scaled_sel"])}
                     for sid in s1.index for key in ("gabor_D", "gabor_U", "flow_left", "flow_right")])
print("\nSelection per session 1 (robust-scaled): candidates above median SNR, 75th-percentile thresholds, ROIs kept:")
print(thr5.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nPer session 1: ROIs, ROIs above median SNR, D sequences, U sequences, left and right flow onsets:", n_sess1)
for scaled in ("scaled", "unscaled"):
    r = rows5[rows5.traces == scaled]
    for p in panels:
        q = r[r.panel == p]
        print(f"{scaled}, panel {p}: planes with selected ROIs {int((q.rois > 0).sum())} of 4; higher after onset {int(q.higher_after.sum())} of 4")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 4, figsize=(13, 10), sharex="col")
for j, (p, (key, tkey)) in enumerate(panels.items()):
    for i, grp in enumerate(groups):
        tr, _ = pooled(grp, key)
        t = R[s1.index[0]]["fig5"][tkey]
        ax = axes[i, j]
        if len(tr):
            m, se = tr.mean(axis=0), tr.std(axis=0, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(tr)) if len(tr) > 1 else 0 * tr[0]
            ax.plot(t, m, color="k")
            ax.fill_between(t, m - se, m + se, color="0.7")
        ax.axvline(0, ls="--", color="0.5")
        ax.set_title(f"{grp}, panel {p}, n = {len(tr)}", fontsize=9)
for ax in axes[-1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("time from D, U or inconsistent flow onset (s)")
fig.supylabel("robust-scaled dF/F, mean +/- SEM over selected ROIs")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
lo_hi = [(pooled(g, k)[0].mean(axis=0).min(), pooled(g, k)[0].mean(axis=0).max()) for k, _ in panels.values() for g in groups if len(pooled(g, k)[0])]
print("Range of the plotted means:", round(min(a for a, _ in lo_hi), 3), "to", round(max(b for _, b in lo_hi), 3))
# Decision rule per plane, under the criterion's three readings of the Gabor panel (answer of 2026-10-22):
# (a) panel a, (b) panel b, (c) both panels; the two flow panels always enter.
readings5 = {"a": ["a"], "b": ["b"], "c": ["a", "b"]}
for scaled in ("scaled", "unscaled"):
    r = rows5[rows5.traces == scaled].set_index(["panel", "group"])
    for name, gab in readings5.items():
        holds = {g: bool(all(r.loc[(p, g), "rois"] > 0 and r.loc[(p, g), "higher_after"] for p in gab + ["c", "d"])) for g in groups}
        n = sum(holds.values())
        out = "reproduced" if n == 4 else "partially reproduced" if n >= 2 else "not reproduced"
        print(f"{scaled}, reading ({name}): rule holds in {n} of 4 planes {holds} -> {out}")

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The selection yields ROIs in every plane for each panel. The flow responses (panels c and d) are higher after inconsistent flow onset in all four planes. For Gabor sequences, panel a (consistent, around D) is higher after onset in 2 of 4 planes; L2/3 and L5 somata are lower (-0.063 and -0.020). Panel b (inconsistent, around U) is higher in 3 of 4; L5 dendrites are at -0.001. The answer of 2026-10-22 says the paper does not give the Gabor panel. The criterion now names three readings and gives the outcome they share, or methods_underspecified if they differ. With robust-scaled traces the rule holds in 2 planes under reading (a), panel a (partially reproduced), and in 3 under reading (b), panel b (partially reproduced). Under reading (c), both panels, it holds in 1 (not reproduced). The readings disagree, so the claim stays blocked, now as the criterion directs. With unscaled dF/F, panel a is higher in 2 of 4 planes and panel b in 4 of 4, and the three readings give partially reproduced (2 planes), reproduced (4) and partially reproduced (2), so they disagree there too. The selection keeps 0 to 58 ROIs per session and panel, from 7 to 818 candidates above the median SNR; mouse 418779 (7 candidates) gives 1 ROI in panels a to c and none in panel d.

fig5-consistent-vs-inconsistent¶

Responses to consistent and inconsistent stimuli differed clearly in the example ROIs.

Gabor: for the ROIs selected on consistent sequences (reading a) or on inconsistent sequences (reading b), the mean over ROIs of their mean trace after D onset and after U onset (0 to 0.6 s), with the SEM across ROIs. Clear when the two differ by more than the sum of their SEMs at some time point.

cvi = []
t = R[s1.index[0]]["fig5"]["gabor_t"]
post = t >= 0
for scaled in ("scaled", "unscaled"):
    for reading, sel_key in (("a", "gabor_D"), ("b", "gabor_U")):
        for grp in groups:
            d, _ = pooled(grp, "gabor_D", scaled, sel_key)
            u, _ = pooled(grp, "gabor_U", scaled, sel_key)
            n = len(d)
            if n < 2:
                cvi.append({"traces": scaled, "reading": reading, "group": grp, "rois": n, "clear": False})
                continue
            md, mu = d.mean(axis=0)[post], u.mean(axis=0)[post]
            sd, su = d.std(axis=0, ddof=1)[post] / np.sqrt(n), u.std(axis=0, ddof=1)[post] / np.sqrt(n)
            gap = np.abs(mu - md) - (sd + su)
            cvi.append({"traces": scaled, "reading": reading, "group": grp, "rois": n,
                        "max_abs_diff": np.abs(mu - md).max(), "sem_sum_there": (sd + su)[np.argmax(gap)],
                        "frames_clear": int((gap > 0).sum()), "frames": int(post.sum()), "clear": bool((gap > 0).any()),
                        "mean_U_minus_D": (mu - md).mean()})
cvi = pd.DataFrame(cvi)
print(cvi.round(4).to_string(index=False))
for scaled in ("scaled", "unscaled"):
    for reading in ("a", "b"):
        q = cvi[(cvi.traces == scaled) & (cvi.reading == reading)]
        print(f"{scaled}, reading ({reading}): planes with a clear difference {int(q.clear.sum())} of 4")
    w = cvi[cvi.traces == scaled].pivot_table(index="group", columns="reading", values="clear", aggfunc="first")
    print(f"{scaled}: planes clear under (a) and (b) at once: {int((w.a & w.b).sum())} of 4 {w[w.a & w.b].index.tolist()}")
# Visual flow: reported, not judged (the selection requires a larger response after onset).
for p in ("c", "d"):

    print(f"flow panel {p}: post minus pre over selected ROIs", dict(zip(q.group, q.post_minus_pre.round(3))))

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified), as it depends on fig5-example-responses. That claim stays blocked after the answer of 2026-10-22, since its three readings disagree. Its own test ran: with robust-scaled traces, the D and U responses of the selected ROIs differ by more than the sum of their SEMs in 2 of 4 planes under reading (a), the ROIs selected on consistent sequences, and in 3 of 4 under reading (b), the ROIs selected on inconsistent sequences. By its criterion this is partially reproduced under both readings, read as at least two planes under each. Read as planes where both readings hold at once, it holds in 1 of 4 (L5 dendrites), which would be not reproduced. The claim stays blocked because the protocol blocks a claim that depends on a blocked claim, for the same reason. The flow differences (post minus pre, 0.030 to 0.206) are reported only, as the selection requires them.

fig7a-snr-stable and fig7b-signal-stable¶

ROI SNR is stable over the three days.

The mean dF/F signal of ROIs is stable over days.

Signal is the mean of the dF/F values above the noise threshold (calculate_snr). Readings: (a) the notches (median +/- 1.57 IQR / sqrt(n)) of the three sessions of a plane overlap pairwise; (b) each session's median lies inside the interquartile range of every other session of the plane.

In [33]:
def stability(col):
    rows = []
    for grp in groups:
        st = {}
        for n in (1, 2, 3):
            v = roi_all[(roi_all.group == grp) & (roi_all.local_n == n)][col].to_numpy()
            q1, med, q3 = np.percentile(v, [25, 50, 75])
            half = 1.57 * (q3 - q1) / np.sqrt(len(v))
            st[n] = (med, q1, q3, med - half, med + half, len(v))
        notch = all(st[a][3] <= st[b][4] and st[b][3] <= st[a][4] for a, b in ((1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)))
        iqr = all(st[b][1] <= st[a][0] <= st[b][2] for a in (1, 2, 3) for b in (1, 2, 3) if a != b)
        rows.append({"group": grp, **{f"median_s{n}": st[n][0] for n in (1, 2, 3)},
                     **{f"notch_s{n}": f"{st[n][3]:.3f}-{st[n][4]:.3f}" for n in (1, 2, 3)},
                     **{f"iqr_s{n}": f"{st[n][1]:.3f}-{st[n][2]:.3f}" for n in (1, 2, 3)},
                     "notches_overlap": notch, "medians_in_iqrs": iqr})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("group")


for col, name in (("snr", "SNR"), ("signal", "signal (dF/F)")):
    stab = stability(col)
    print(f"{name}:")

          f" under both: {int((stab.notches_overlap & stab.medians_in_iqrs).sum())} of 4\n")

Result: both blocked (methods_underspecified), as their readings disagree. For SNR, every session's median lies inside the other sessions' interquartile ranges in all four planes (reading b). The notches overlap pairwise in only 2 of 4 planes (reading a); in L2/3 and L5 dendrites, whose sessions hold 648 to 2807 ROIs, the notches are narrow and the medians drift by 0.016 and 0.033. For signal, reading (b) holds in 4 of 4 planes and reading (a) in 1 of 4. Under reading (a) both claims would be not reproduced, under (b) reproduced. The criteria name methods_underspecified for this case.

fig7c-correlations-similar and fig7c-high-correlation-fraction¶

The distributions of pairwise ROI correlations are very similar for apical dendrite ROIs and somatic ROIs, which suggests the dendrites are not heavily over-segmented.

About 0.01% of possible pairs of L2/3 dendritic ROIs have correlations above 0.8.

Pearson correlation of every pair of ROIs within a session, on full-session dF/F smoothed with a centred 4-point moving average (mode mirror), pooled over mice per line, plane and session. Similar: medians, and 95th percentiles, of the dendritic and somatic distributions of the same line and session differ by less than (a) 0.05 or (b) 0.1.

Result: fig7c-correlations-similar blocked (methods_underspecified), as its readings disagree; fig7c-high-correlation-fraction blocked as it depends on it. The dendritic and somatic medians differ by 0.006 to 0.025 and the 95th percentiles by 0.049 to 0.089. That is similar for 6 of 6 comparisons under reading (b), 0.1, and for 1 of 6 under reading (a), 0.05. For the high correlations, the analysed L2/3 dendritic sessions come from the two mice the criterion now names (413663 and 433414, answer of 2026-10-22). Pooled over them, 0.0178% of pairs exceed 0.8 (134 of 752101, reading a), and the mean of the three sessions is 0.0176% (reading b). By local session they are 0.0211, 0.0276 and 0.0043% (reading c), so not every session is within tolerance. None of the three readings is within 0.005 to 0.015%, so the claim would not be reproduced if its dependency were decided. It stays blocked because the protocol blocks a claim that depends on a blocked claim, for the same reason. The answer rules out per-mouse sessions as a reading, so the two mouse sessions inside the band (0.0054 and 0.0067%) no longer bear on the outcome. r >= 0.8 gives the same counts.

fig7a-source-link¶

The per-ROI SNRs computed from the dataset agree with those in the source data of Figure 7a in the paper's repository.

In [35]:
src = oc.fig7a_source()
src["sessids"] = src.sessids.astype(int).astype(str)
link = []
for _, r in src.iterrows():
    sid = r.sessids
    mine = R[sid]["roi"].snr.to_numpy() if sid in R else np.array([])
    theirs = np.asarray(r.snrs, dtype=float)
    same_n = len(mine) == len(theirs)
    rel = np.abs(mine - theirs) / np.abs(theirs) if same_n else np.array([np.nan])
    link.append({"session": sid, "in_dataset": sid in R, "rois_source": len(theirs), "rois_dataset": len(mine),
                 "frac_within_1pct": np.mean(rel <= 0.01) if same_n else np.nan, "max_rel_diff": np.nanmax(rel)})
link = pd.DataFrame(link).set_index("session")
link["ok"] = (link.rois_source == link.rois_dataset) & (link.frac_within_1pct >= 0.95)
print(link.to_string())
print("Source sessions:", len(link), "; in the analysed set:", int(link.index.isin(sess.index[sess.analysed]).sum()),
      "; sessions meeting the rule:", int(link.ok.sum()))

fig9-onset-offset-transients¶

Mean dF/F responses across ROIs show distinct transients aligned to stimulus onsets (grey screen to stimulus) and offsets (stimulus to grey screen), which validates the temporal alignment of stimuli and recordings.

Onsets are the ends of every grey period but the last, offsets the starts of every grey period but the first, -2 to 2 s around each. Per ROI, the mean trace over transitions; then mean and SEM across ROIs pooled over mice per line, plane and session. A group shows a transient when at some time in 0 to 2 s the mean differs from its mean over -2 to 0 s by more than k SEM. Readings: transitions (a) all, (b) Gabor only; k 1 or 2. Robust-scaled dF/F; unscaled as a variant.

In [36]:
def transient_table(scaled):
    rows = []
    for grp in groups:
        for n in (1, 2, 3):
            sids = sess.index[sess.analysed & (sess.group == grp) & (sess.local_n == n)]
            for kind in ("onset", "offset"):
                for reading in ("a", "b"):
                    per_roi = []
                    for sid in sids:
                        tr = R[sid]["transitions"]
                        sel = (tr.kind == kind) & ((reading == "a") | (tr.stimulus == "gabors"))
                        per_roi.append(R[sid][f"trans_{scaled}"][:, sel.to_numpy()].mean(axis=1))
                    x = np.concatenate(per_roi)
                    t = R[sids[0]]["trans_t"]
                    m, se = x.mean(axis=0), x.std(axis=0, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(x))
                    base = m[t < 0].mean()
                    z = np.abs(m[t >= 0] - base) / se[t >= 0]
                    rows.append({"traces": scaled, "group": grp, "session": n, "kind": kind, "reading": reading,
                                 "rois": len(x), "max_dev_in_sem": z.max(), "k1": bool((z > 1).any()), "k2": bool((z > 2).any()),
                                 "peak_change": (m[t >= 0] - base)[np.argmax(z)]})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


for scaled in ("scaled", "unscaled"):
    tt9 = transient_table(scaled)
    wide = tt9.pivot_table(index=["group", "session"], columns=["kind", "reading"], values="max_dev_in_sem")
    print(f"{scaled} dF/F, largest deviation from baseline in 0 to 2 s, in SEMs:")
    print(wide.round(2).to_string())
    for reading in ("a", "b"):
        for k in ("k1", "k2"):
            q = tt9[tt9.reading == reading]
            both = q.pivot_table(index=["group", "session"], columns="kind", values=k).all(axis=1)
            print(f"  reading ({reading}), {k}: groups with a transient at onset and at offset {int(both.sum())} of 12")
    print()
pm9 = []
for sid in sess.index[sess.analysed]:
    tr, t = R[sid]["transitions"], R[sid]["trans_t"]
    row = {"session_id": sid, "group": sess.group[sid], "mouse": sess.subject[sid], "session": sess.local_n[sid], "rois": R[sid]["n_rois"]}
    for kind in ("onset", "offset"):
        x = R[sid]["trans_scaled"][:, (tr.kind == kind).to_numpy()].mean(axis=1)
        if len(x) > 1:
            m, se = x.mean(axis=0), x.std(axis=0, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(x))
            row[kind] = (np.abs(m[t >= 0] - m[t < 0].mean()) / se[t >= 0]).max()
    pm9.append(row)
pm9 = pd.DataFrame(pm9)
print("Per mouse and session, reading (a), robust-scaled: largest deviation in SEMs over that mouse's ROIs")
print(pm9.round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("Range over mouse sessions (SEMs):", round(min(pm9.onset.min(), pm9.offset.min()), 2), "to",
      round(max(pm9.onset.max(), pm9.offset.max()), 2))
unshown = clock.index[clock.true <= clock.null_p99]

Result: reproduced. In all 12 groups the mean robust-scaled response departs from its pre-transition mean by more than 2 SEM, at both onset and offset. With all transitions (reading a) the largest deviations are 8.8 to 35.3 SEM, and with Gabor transitions only (reading b) 2.3 to 12.8 SEM, so it holds under every reading. Unscaled dF/F gives 2.1 to 32.6 SEM, and every mouse session taken alone gives 4.1 to 30.2 SEM (reading a). The analysed session whose alignment the clock check did not establish, 777496949 (418779 session 1, 15 ROIs), deviates by 4.07 SEM at onset and 6.77 at offset.

file-sizes and download-33-files¶

Each session has three file versions; basic files are about 130 MB to 1.7 GB, the stimulus images add about 1.5 GB, and the motion-corrected stack adds about 45 GB.

The basic files of the sessions 1 to 3 that passed QC are 33 files totalling about 15 GB.

In [37]:
sz = assets.dropna(subset=["kind"]).pivot_table(index="session", columns="kind", values="size", aggfunc="first")
print("Sessions with all three versions:", int(sz.notna().all(axis=1).sum()), "of", len(sz))
for unit, mb, gb in (("decimal", 1e6, 1e9), ("binary", 2**20, 2**30)):
    vals = {"smallest basic (MB)": sz.B.min() / mb, "largest basic (GB)": sz.B.max() / gb,
            "I minus B, median (GB)": (sz.I - sz.B).median() / gb, "S minus I, median (GB)": (sz.S - sz.I).median() / gb}
    exp = {"smallest basic (MB)": (130, 13), "largest basic (GB)": (1.7, 0.17), "I minus B, median (GB)": (1.5, 0.15),
           "S minus I, median (GB)": (45, 4.5)}
    within = {k: abs(v - exp[k][0]) <= exp[k][1] for k, v in vals.items()}
    print(f"{unit}:", {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in vals.items()}, "; within tolerance:", within, "; all:", all(within.values()))
print("I minus B range (GB, decimal):", round((sz.I - sz.B).min() / 1e9, 3), "to", round((sz.I - sz.B).max() / 1e9, 3),
      "; S minus I range:", round((sz.S - sz.I).min() / 1e9, 2), "to", round((sz.S - sz.I).max() / 1e9, 2))
sel33 = sz.loc[sess.index[sess.analysed]]
print("\nBasic files of local sessions 1 to 3 passing QC:", len(sel33), "; total", round(sel33.B.sum() / 1e9, 2), "GB decimal,",
      round(sel33.B.sum() / 2**30, 2), "GB binary (expected 15 +/- 1.5)")

Result: both reproduced. Every session has the three file versions. In decimal units the basic files run from 136.7 MB to 1.70 GB, the stimulus images add a median of 1.49 GB and the imaging stack a median of 45.5 GB; in binary units 130.3 MB, 1.59 GB, 1.39 GB and 42.3 GB. All are within tolerance in both. The 33 basic files of local sessions 1 to 3 that passed QC total 14.82 GB (13.80 GiB).

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The 33 analysed sessions are selected with the QC results and local session numbers of Supplementary Table 1, as the dataset holds no QC; the local numbers equal the order of the start times in the files. Table 1 and Table 2 values are read from Supplementary Table 1, which agrees with the paper's tables. Windows around events are taken as whole two-photon frames from the trial table's frame numbers, which is a standard choice. All ROIs in each file are used, as in the paper's code.

What was found about the dataset.

  • The session start times are stated with a Pacific offset (-07:00 or -08:00), but their clock values are those Supplementary Table 1 gives as UTC. For four sessions this puts the date a day after the date in Table 2, and the date of birth implied by the age of mouse 418779 a day after Table 1's. The files hold no other wall-clock time to tell which is right.
  • The three sessions of mouse 433414 are recorded at a depth of 60 um; Tables 2 and S1 give 75 um.
  • The files hold no QC result, local session number or stimulus seed. The paper's analyses use only sessions that passed QC, and the dandiset's description points to an outside table for them. No small dataset or attribute under general, or at the files' top level, mentions QC.
  • The dF/F of the 28 dendritic sessions is stored gzip-chunked in small chunks, which makes streaming it through h5py slow; the somatic files store it contiguous.
  • The plane (somata or dendrites) is not recorded; it follows from the depth.
  • Square size and speed are given in pixels of the unwarped stimulus, without the geometry needed to convert them to the degrees the paper states.
  • The clock check fails in two sessions (777496949, 15 ROIs; 838633305, failed QC).
